**Dane Lloyd**MP (born February 16, 1991) is a Canadian politician who was elected to the House of Commons of Canada in a by-election on October 23, 2017, following the resignation of Rona Ambrose.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-edrona-2) Lloyd represents the constituency of Parkland as a member of the Conservative Party of Canada. Lloyd continues to serve as a Canadian Armyreservist in the [Governor General's Foot Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_General's_Foot_Guards "Governor General's Foot Guards") located in Ottawa.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-danehuff-3) As of 2024 he held a commission as an infantry officer with the rank of captain.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-About_-_Dane_Lloyd_MP-1)
Lloyd was born in St. Albert, Alberta, and raised outside Spruce Grove, Alberta, where his family farms.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-gazette-4) He attended and graduated from Edmonton Christian High School in 2009. In 2014, he graduated from Trinity Western University with a Bachelor of Arts degree in history and political science.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-DaneLinkedIn-5) While completing his undergraduate studies, Lloyd was elected vice president of Academic Affairs for the Trinity Western University Student Association. He attended the Laurentian Leadership Centre in Ottawa, and served as President of the Trinity Western Model United Nations Society.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-DaneLinkedIn-5)

Lloyd began his political career as an intern serving in the office of MP Brent Rathgeber in 2009. The following year he served in the office of Tony Clement then Minister of Industry. His final internship in the fall of 2011 through the Laurentian Leadership Centre was in the office of Jason Kenney when he served as Minister of Citizenship and Immigration. In 2013 before completing his degree Lloyd moved from Alberta to Ottawa and served as a special assistant to then Minister of International Trade (Ed Fast). After the 2015 election Lloyd accepted a position as parliamentary advisor to St. Albert—Edmonton MP Michael Cooper.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-danehuff-3) In early 2016, Lloyd accepted a commission as an infantry officer in the [Governor General's Foot Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_General's_Foot_Guards "Governor General's Foot Guards").
After he won the by-election in Sturgeon River—Parkland in the fall of 2017, Lloyd served on several Parliamentary Committees including the Standing Committee on Industry, Science and Technology; the Special Committee on the COVID-19 pandemic; and the Standing Committee on Veterans Affairs. Lloyd currently serves on the Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-ourcom-6)
In 2020, Conservative leader [Erin O'Toole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_O'Toole "Erin O'Toole") appointed Lloyd as Shadow Minister for Digital Government.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-7) Following the 2021 election Lloyd was appointed as Shadow Minister for Emergency Preparedness.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-8)
On 25 February 2022 interim leader Candice Bergen re-named Lloyd to shadow the Minister of Emergency Preparedness.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-cawpa-9)

On October 12, 2022, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre re-appointed Lloyd to the position of Shadow Minister of Emergency Preparedness, a position he holds to this day.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-10)
Federal ridings in Alberta were redistributed prior to the 2025 federal election; Lloyd was re-elected to parliament in the newly created Parkland riding.

#### Legislative initiatives
[edit]
During his nomination for the Conservative Party of Canada in 2017, Lloyd proposed introducing McCanns' Law in honour of St. Albert residents Lyle and Marie McCann who went missing in July 2010 on a road trip from their home town to Chilliwack, British Columbia.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-11) Their charred motor home was discovered a few days later, resulting in a search that led to the arrest (and subsequent conviction[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-chalb-12)) of Travis Vader for their murder.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-ejvader-13) While Vader was still unwilling to assist authorities in locating the McCanns' remains he will be eligible for parole in 2021.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-chalb-12) This was the catalyst for Lloyd's commitment, in the 2017 Sturgeon River-Parkland Conservative Nomination, to introduce a Private Member's Bill that would help families recover the remains of their loved ones.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-nobody-14) The McCann's oldest son, Bret McCann, worked with Lloyd in drafting of the bill after he was elected.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-mccson-15)
In March 2019, Lloyd introduced Private Member's Bill C-437, An Act to amend the Criminal Code, the Corrections and Conditional Release Act and the Prisons and Reformatories Act, also known as **McCanns' Law**. If passed, willingness to assist authorities to locate the remains of the victim(s) would be a consideration for parole eligibility for someone convicted in the death of a person. According to Lloyd "the hope is not to necessarily punish people more, but to give them (an) incentive to cooperate, to give relevant information on the location of the bodies and then enable the families to have the closure of a funeral."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-stalim-16)

R&B singer Lloyd (Lloyd Polite Jr.) was born in New Orleans, Louisiana to parents Robin Lewis Polite and Lloyd Polite Sr. His father, Lloyd Polite Sr., tragically passed away when Lloyd was a young child, after which he and his family relocated from New Orleans, Louisiana, to Decatur, Georgia when he was 2, following the murder of his father.   
Lloyd is African-American, with additional Louisiana Creole, Scottish, and Filipino heritage.
Lloyd's music career kicked off with the group N-Toon (which also included his younger brother Chuckie). The group disbanded when he was 14, after about 4 years, but Lloyd continued to make music on his own. In 2004, he released his debut single and album, "Southside," under Murder Inc. Records. The single featured label-mate and singer-songwriter Ashanti.
Lloyd followed with 2007's, "Street Love," which featured mega-hit single, "You," with rapper Lil' Wayne. The song peaked at #1 on Billboard's Hot R&B/Hip-Hop chart and #9 on their Hot 100 chart; it is still one of the most played and requested songs from his catalog. After releasing his third album and fourth albums, "Lessons in Love" (2008) and "King of Hearts" (2011), Lloyd took some time away from music to focus on family and school. He reemerged in 2016 with "Tru," an intimate bluesy record that revealed a lot of the artists' thoughts, feelings, and struggles. The single appeared on an EP and LP of the same name, released in 2016 and 2018, respectively.
In 2019, Lloyd joined an all-star lineup of artists for The Millennium Tour, which made its way around the US from March-May 2019. He also appeared in TV One's season three premiere of "Unsung," and made his film debut in the network's original biopic, "The Bobby Debarge Story."
Lloyd continues his career as a touring artist and independent musician, maintaining steady activity on nostalgia tours like the R&B Music Experience.

**Dane Lloyd**MP (born February 16, 1991) is a Canadian politician who was elected to the House of Commons of Canada in a by-election on October 23, 2017, following the resignation of Rona Ambrose.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-edrona-2) Lloyd represents the constituency of Parkland as a member of the Conservative Party of Canada. Lloyd continues to serve as a Canadian Armyreservist in the [Governor General's Foot Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_General's_Foot_Guards "Governor General's Foot Guards") located in Ottawa.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-danehuff-3) As of 2024 he held a commission as an infantry officer with the rank of captain.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-About_-_Dane_Lloyd_MP-1)
Lloyd was born in St. Albert, Alberta, and raised outside Spruce Grove, Alberta, where his family farms.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-gazette-4) He attended and graduated from Edmonton Christian High School in 2009. In 2014, he graduated from Trinity Western University with a Bachelor of Arts degree in history and political science.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-DaneLinkedIn-5) While completing his undergraduate studies, Lloyd was elected vice president of Academic Affairs for the Trinity Western University Student Association. He attended the Laurentian Leadership Centre in Ottawa, and served as President of the Trinity Western Model United Nations Society.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-DaneLinkedIn-5)

Lloyd began his political career as an intern serving in the office of MP Brent Rathgeber in 2009. The following year he served in the office of Tony Clement then Minister of Industry. His final internship in the fall of 2011 through the Laurentian Leadership Centre was in the office of Jason Kenney when he served as Minister of Citizenship and Immigration. In 2013 before completing his degree Lloyd moved from Alberta to Ottawa and served as a special assistant to then Minister of International Trade (Ed Fast). After the 2015 election Lloyd accepted a position as parliamentary advisor to St. Albert—Edmonton MP Michael Cooper.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-danehuff-3) In early 2016, Lloyd accepted a commission as an infantry officer in the [Governor General's Foot Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_General's_Foot_Guards "Governor General's Foot Guards").
After he won the by-election in Sturgeon River—Parkland in the fall of 2017, Lloyd served on several Parliamentary Committees including the Standing Committee on Industry, Science and Technology; the Special Committee on the COVID-19 pandemic; and the Standing Committee on Veterans Affairs. Lloyd currently serves on the Standing Committee on Public Safety and National Security[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-ourcom-6)
In 2020, Conservative leader [Erin O'Toole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erin_O'Toole "Erin O'Toole") appointed Lloyd as Shadow Minister for Digital Government.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-7) Following the 2021 election Lloyd was appointed as Shadow Minister for Emergency Preparedness.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-8)
On 25 February 2022 interim leader Candice Bergen re-named Lloyd to shadow the Minister of Emergency Preparedness.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-cawpa-9)

On October 12, 2022, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre re-appointed Lloyd to the position of Shadow Minister of Emergency Preparedness, a position he holds to this day.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-10)
Federal ridings in Alberta were redistributed prior to the 2025 federal election; Lloyd was re-elected to parliament in the newly created Parkland riding.

#### Legislative initiatives
[edit]
During his nomination for the Conservative Party of Canada in 2017, Lloyd proposed introducing McCanns' Law in honour of St. Albert residents Lyle and Marie McCann who went missing in July 2010 on a road trip from their home town to Chilliwack, British Columbia.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-11) Their charred motor home was discovered a few days later, resulting in a search that led to the arrest (and subsequent conviction[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-chalb-12)) of Travis Vader for their murder.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-ejvader-13) While Vader was still unwilling to assist authorities in locating the McCanns' remains he will be eligible for parole in 2021.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-chalb-12) This was the catalyst for Lloyd's commitment, in the 2017 Sturgeon River-Parkland Conservative Nomination, to introduce a Private Member's Bill that would help families recover the remains of their loved ones.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-nobody-14) The McCann's oldest son, Bret McCann, worked with Lloyd in drafting of the bill after he was elected.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-mccson-15)
In March 2019, Lloyd introduced Private Member's Bill C-437, An Act to amend the Criminal Code, the Corrections and Conditional Release Act and the Prisons and Reformatories Act, also known as **McCanns' Law**. If passed, willingness to assist authorities to locate the remains of the victim(s) would be a consideration for parole eligibility for someone convicted in the death of a person. According to Lloyd "the hope is not to necessarily punish people more, but to give them (an) incentive to cooperate, to give relevant information on the location of the bodies and then enable the families to have the closure of a funeral."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dane_Lloyd#cite_note-stalim-16)

# Lloyd Dane
**Lloyd Dane** (August 19, 1925 – December 11, 2015) was an American NASCAR Grand National Series driver from Eldon, Missouri.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-RacingReference-1) He participated part-time in the 1951 and 1954 to 1964 seasons, capturing four wins, all in his own car.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-RacingReference-1) Two of Dane's wins came during the 1956 season, when he finished 23rd in points.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-RacingReference-1)
Dane first started racing in 1949 and was the first NASCAR Pacific Coast Late Model Series champion; he took the championship in 1954, 1956 and 1957.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-2) He was noted for driving a Hudson Hornet, which he drove to his 1954 championship, along with longtime friend Tim Flock.

Lloyd
Dane Wells, age 66 of Bolivar, MO, passed away May 7, 2013, at Citizens
Memorial Hospital. Lloyd was born January
10, 1947, in Slagle, MO, to Virgil and Emma (Slagle) Wells, the youngest of
three children. He is a US Air Force
Viet Nam veteran. Lloyd was united in
marriage to Tania Palacios December 3, 1997.
Lloyd was saved at an early age at Union Grove Missionary Baptist
Church, and was a member of the Slagle Missionary Baptist Church.
He
was a loving husband, father, and brother, and tried to do as much as he
could. Dane was passionate about his
coin collection, and loved to fish.
He
was preceded in death by his parents.
He
is survived by his wife Tania Wells of the home; three daughters: Janet, and
Mitzy of FL, and Brandy Wells of the home; four granddaughters; two sisters: Wilma
Jean Graves of Bolivar, MO, and Rosie Graves and husband Clarence of
Morrisville, MO; as well as other relatives and friends.
Funeral services will be held at 2:00 PM Friday,
10, 2013, at Pitts Chapel with Bro. Ray Graves officiating. Burial will follow at Slagle Cemetery. Visitation will be held Thursday, May 9,
2013, from 6:00 to 7:00 PM in the funeral home.
Arrangements have been entrusted to Pitts Chapel Bolivar, MO.

# Lloyd Dane
**Lloyd Dane** (August 19, 1925 – December 11, 2015) was an American NASCAR Grand National Series driver from Eldon, Missouri.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-RacingReference-1) He participated part-time in the 1951 and 1954 to 1964 seasons, capturing four wins, all in his own car.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-RacingReference-1) Two of Dane's wins came during the 1956 season, when he finished 23rd in points.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-RacingReference-1)
Dane first started racing in 1949 and was the first NASCAR Pacific Coast Late Model Series champion; he took the championship in 1954, 1956 and 1957.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lloyd_Dane#cite_note-2) He was noted for driving a Hudson Hornet, which he drove to his 1954 championship, along with longtime friend Tim Flock.

Lloyd
Dane Wells, age 66 of Bolivar, MO, passed away May 7, 2013, at Citizens
Memorial Hospital. Lloyd was born January
10, 1947, in Slagle, MO, to Virgil and Emma (Slagle) Wells, the youngest of
three children. He is a US Air Force
Viet Nam veteran. Lloyd was united in
marriage to Tania Palacios December 3, 1997.
Lloyd was saved at an early age at Union Grove Missionary Baptist
Church, and was a member of the Slagle Missionary Baptist Church.
He
was a loving husband, father, and brother, and tried to do as much as he
could. Dane was passionate about his
coin collection, and loved to fish.
He
was preceded in death by his parents.
He
is survived by his wife Tania Wells of the home; three daughters: Janet, and
Mitzy of FL, and Brandy Wells of the home; four granddaughters; two sisters: Wilma
Jean Graves of Bolivar, MO, and Rosie Graves and husband Clarence of
Morrisville, MO; as well as other relatives and friends.
Funeral services will be held at 2:00 PM Friday,
10, 2013, at Pitts Chapel with Bro. Ray Graves officiating. Burial will follow at Slagle Cemetery. Visitation will be held Thursday, May 9,
2013, from 6:00 to 7:00 PM in the funeral home.
Arrangements have been entrusted to Pitts Chapel Bolivar, MO.

**Eldon** is a city in Miller County, Missouri, United States, located 30 miles (48 km) southwest of Jefferson City. The population was 4,416 as of the 2020 census.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldon,_Missouri#cite_note-Census_2020-3)
Eldon was platted in 1881, and according to tradition, named after a railroad official.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldon,_Missouri#cite_note-5) The railroad closed down in 1980 and is proposed to be transformed into the extension of the Rock Island Trail. A post office called Eldon has been in operation since 1881.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldon,_Missouri#cite_note-6)
On the night of May 22, 2019, a tornado touched down west of Eldon. It came through Eldon damaging many homes and businesses. The same tornado struck Jefferson City later in the evening.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldon,_Missouri#cite_note-7)
Eldon is in northwestern Miller County. The city is served by U.S. Route 54 and Missouri Routes 52 and 87. Jefferson City is 30 miles (48 km) to the northeast, while the city of Lake Ozark is 12 miles (19 km) to the south. Bagnell Dam, which forms the Lake of the Ozarks, is 11 miles (18 km) south of Eldon.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldon,_Missouri#cite_note-8)

According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the city of Eldon has a total area of 3.56 square miles (9.22 km 2), all land.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldon,_Missouri#cite_note-CenPopGazetteer2023-1) The city sits on high ground: the northwest side of the city drains toward South Moreau Creek, part of the Moreau River watershed flowing to the Missouri River, while the northeast side of the city is the source of Blythes Creek, a tributary of South Moreau Creek. The southeast side of Eldon drains into Saline Creek, a tributary of the Osage River, which in turn flows northeastern to the Missouri River.

History of Eldon - News Tribune ### ELDON, MILLER COUNTY'S LARGEST TOWN, IS ONE OF THE YOUNGEST #### By Peggy Smith Hake

# Eldon Community - Miller County Historical Society
Miller County became a reality in 1837 and for many years had very few towns within its borders. In 1850, there were only 4 towns ... Tuscumbia, Iberia, Mt. Pleasant, and Rocky Mount. A map of the county, dated 1875, still only shows Tuscumbia, Iberia, Mt. Pleasant and Rocky Mount. There were small post office settlements throughout the county, but no other established towns. By 1905, a county map shows the towns of Olean, Spring Garden, Etterville, Mt. Pleasant, Rocky Mount, Eldon, Aurora Springs, Bagnell, Tuscumbia, Mary's Home, Charles/St. Elizabeth, Ulmans Ridge, Brumley and Iberia. The town of Eldon was platted 15 March 1882 when it became apparent the railroad would be built there and not at Aurora Springs, which was the county's 'boom town' during those days. George Riley Weeks, a Civil War veteran, came to Miller Co. circa 1867 from the state of Vermont. George brought his wife, Almira (Joslyn) Weeks and two children to Missouri following the war. Typical of other pioneer families, George and Almira decided they would like to see the "wild and wooly west". When they settled in northern Miller Co., in Saline Township, they bought land northeast of present day Eldon and built a log cabin as their first Missouri home. Later he bought more land north of Eldon and built a larger frame home for his family. George and Almira had two other children after coming to Missouri, twin daughters, but both died young. George Weeks continued to buy many acres in what is today the city of Eldon. When it was determined that a railroad would be built through the area north of Aurora Springs, George decided to layout and plat a new town to surround the proposed railroad tracks. When the old Missouri Pacific Line (called the Jefferson City, Lebanon, and Southwest railroad) was constructed through northern Miller County, George donated land to the railway company to build a depot. George Weeks platted the original town of Eldon to contain 109 blocks. The streets, named by George, included: Mill, Maple, Oak, Aurora, Pine, Spruce, Broadway, Locust, Grand, Chestnut, and Walnut (all running north and south).

# Eldon Community - Miller County Historical Society
The streets which ran east and west were First Street to Fifteenth Street. By 1905, Eldon had two railroads, the Missouri Pacific, with a depot at Second & Maple Streets, and the Chicago, Rock Island, and Pacific with its depot located at the corner of Sixth & Maple Streets. George Weeks and Isaac Newton built the Eldon Roller Mills on the site of Gerbes Supermarket. The mill 'fired' and built the bricks for their own use at the mill. Behind the mill building was an old mill pond but today there is no evidence of the pond. George Riley Weeks (1838-1910) and his wife, Almira (1840-1928) looked beyond their life span in the late 19th century and laid out the future on a parchment sheet when they platted the new town of Eldon in 1882. No one seems to know for a certainty why the name Eldon was chosen. Legend says it was in honor of an English nobleman named Lord Eldon ... if so, he would be proud to see the little city which carries his name today in the late 20th century. NOTE: Sincere thanks to Freda Walker Weeks of Eldon for the above information concerning the beginning of the city of Eldon.
